comment: The consent-seal wire, read by BOTH sides: app/src-tauri/src/consent_seal_tests.rs deserializes 'request' into RecordScriptConsentRequest (deny_unknown_fields, so 'inputs' with its caller-side extras is REFUSED) and serializes a ScriptConsentList that must equal 'response'; app/src/api/__tests__/distributedConsentSealedWire.test.ts asserts recordConsent sends exactly 'request' for 'inputs' (the extras, a planted sourceHash among them, never leave the page), and that 'response' is what a typed ConsentReport literal spells. A field renamed on either side turns one of them red.

buttonAction.comment: An approval of BUTTON code: its id is 'buttonAction:' + sha256 of its exact bytes, so an id must name the source beside it. Rust (consent_seal_tests.rs, a_button_action_approval_must_name_the_bytes_it_shows) accepts 'matched' and refuses 'mismatched' (the id names the bytes of 'Report();' while the source is 'Exfiltrate();'); the TypeScript double (helpers/consentStoreDouble.ts) mirrors that refusal, and distributedConsentSealedWire.test.ts asserts both through recordConsent.
